title: ConstraintSet
description:
Hard and advisory sequence constraints, plus the repair policy.

ACTIONABLE VS PRE-EXISTING VIOLATIONS. A blocking violation confined to immutable sequence — a repeat between two backbone regions, a restriction site in the vector — is real but is a property of the INPUT, not of any candidate. The search engine cannot edit it, so counting it against every candidate would report every design as infeasible and give the search nothing to optimize toward. Such violations are reported once, at submission, by the feasibility analyser (CF-FEAS-001); per-candidate feasibility considers only violations that touch an editable position. This distinction was surfaced by the P1-27 differential against the legacy prototype; see docs/legacy-parity.md.

TWO CLASSES, AND THE DISTINCTION IS OPERATIONAL. A `blocking` constraint makes the construct unbuildable (a BsaI site in a Golden Gate assembly; a 20-mer repeat a synthesis vendor will refuse). An `advisory` constraint is a preference that participates in the objective vector instead (GC drifting toward 65%). The search engine treats them completely differently: blocking constraints drive constraint-domination and repair; advisory ones are just terms. Conflating them is the classic failure that makes a codon optimizer return nothing.

The repair policy lives here, not in the search config, because repair budget is a property of how tight the constraints are.

derived_from.description: Provenance of the constraint list. `auto_detected` mirrors the prototype's motif scan and MUST be reported to the user, because a constraint the user did not ask for changing the answer is otherwise inexplicable.

scope.description: `construct` counts occurrences across the whole assembled sequence including immutable backbone, which is the only correct scope for repeat constraints.

motif.description: IUPAC-extended. Expanded to a DFA at load time so detection is O(n) over the sequence.

count_overlapping.description: True reproduces the prototype's count_overlapping() semantics. Naive str.count() undercounts tandem repeats, which is exactly the case a synthesis vendor rejects.

canonical_strand.description: When true, a k-mer and its reverse complement are counted as one, which is the right model for synthesis-complexity scoring.

engine.description: Pinning the engine matters: a dG threshold from ViennaRNA is not the same number as one from the native window kernel.

min_relative_adaptiveness.description: Excludes codons below this w_i. The blunt classic 'ban rare codons' rule; kept because users ask for it, marked advisory by default because AMD-007 argues it is usually counterproductive.

repair_policy.description: Bounds on the repair operator. Every bound is finite by construction: an unbounded repair search is the mechanism by which a repair operator starves the evolutionary loop.

max_window_codons.description: Initial half-width of the codon window searched around a violation.

max_escalations.description: Window doublings before giving up and marking the individual infeasible.

max_depth.description: Maximum number of simultaneous codon substitutions considered.

tabu_tenure_generations.description: How long a (position, codon) pair reverted by repair is discouraged in the mutation operator. This is the concrete anti-thrashing mechanism required by BRIEF-2.3-f.

objective_aware.description: When true, repair breaks ties by least objective degradation using a caller-supplied exact delta table.

stochastic_tie_break.description: Randomized tie-breaking preserves population diversity; deterministic repair collapses the population onto one point on the feasible manifold.

lamarckian.description: Repaired genotype replaces the original. See 06-constraint-repair.md for why, and for the Baldwinian alternative.
